A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SafeSci work. The main text, figures, tables and Appendices A–D are readable and matchable despite added policy sections and renumbered appendix tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 24 LLMs, fine-tuning experiments and over-refusal measurements in Tables 3–7 and Figures 4–5.

after.justification: v2 retains the original model evaluations, fine-tuning results and over-refusal measurements in Tables 3–7 and Figures 4–5.

M1.justification: The template-based and agent-based dataset construction, knowledge/risk distinction, evaluation procedures and LoRA fine-tuning method remain unchanged. The new access tiers govern distribution rather than changing the method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same datasets, seven fields and task coverage. New Table 8 reorganizes existing tasks into access tiers, retaining their sample counts; it does not introduce or remove training or evaluation scenarios.

E2.justification: The evaluated model sets in Tables 3–7 and Figures 4–5 are unchanged, including the three models used for fine-tuning comparisons. The added discussion of prior work introduces no evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1 and 4.3 retain the same prompting, token limits, temperature, sampling, metrics and fine-tuning settings. The appendix answer-availability flag changes for Che.7, but its safety-rate metric and refusal example remain unchanged; no testing-procedure change is documented.

E4.justification: The domain-level, generation, fine-tuning and over-refusal analyses are unchanged, as are the appendix examples. The new risk discussion contains no additional empirical robustness test, ablation or case study.

E5.justification: Both versions report five random samplings of 3,000 questions and the same mean-and-standard-deviation reporting in Tables 3, 5 and 7. No run-count, seed or uncertainty-estimation changes are introduced.

E6.justification: The numerical results and reported findings in Tables 3–7, Figures 4–5 and their accompanying discussion are unchanged. New Table 8 redisplays existing task counts with access classifications, rather than adding experimental outcomes.

T1.justification: The metric descriptions and conceptual assumptions remain unchanged. Neither the new policy sections nor the appendices add or revise mathematical definitions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same dataset contributions, model-evaluation claims, fine-tuning benefits and context-dependent view of scientific safety. The new distribution restrictions do not revise these core claims.

C2.justification: Sections 7–8 newly explain how aggregating public scientific information can lower barriers to misuse and acknowledge benchmark gaming and evaluation-awareness risks. They add a qualitative argument for controlled release, while the existing performance interpretations and over-refusal limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Where v1 provides code/data links, v2 adds extensive access instructions: two task-level tiers, manually reviewed applications, additional email approval for high-risk tasks, non-commercial-use and redistribution restrictions, and access logging/revocation. These substantially change the documented conditions for obtaining and reusing the dataset. Appendix A also changes Che.7's answer-availability flag from yes to no, without establishing that the underlying experiment changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Nguyen et al. (2025), Probing and Steering Evaluation Awareness of Language Models, to support the new limitation discussion. It also invokes WMDP as a precedent for controlled release; the original related-work comparisons remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 appends Section 7, Ethics Statement, and Section 8, Dataset Policy and Risk Disclosure, after the conclusion, using additional subheadings and numbered conditions. The existing scientific narrative and appendix prose undergo no broad rewriting or reorganization.

P2.justification: v2 adds a full-page Task Access Overview as Table 8, grouping existing tasks by access tier. Appendix Tables 8–14 become Tables 9–15 and later material shifts pages; the existing figures and experimental table layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Sections 7–8 and Table 8 provide a limited improvement in transparency by documenting access procedures and explicitly acknowledging misuse and evaluation-awareness risks that v1 did not address in this detail. Experimental support remains unchanged. The benefit is tempered by the newly stated restrictions on reuse and their unresolved tension with the retained open-source description; the PDFs do not demonstrate the effectiveness of the safeguards.
